title: What is known about 1RB0LD_1RC0RF_1LA1RF_0LA0RE_1LD---_0RA0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LD_1RC0RF_1LA1RF_0LA0RE_1LD---_0RA0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. At each new cell on the growing (right) end the tape is 6 3^x1 9 3^x2 9 … 9 3^xm TAIL read from the far end: segments of 111-blocks cut by markers 1^9. Per cycle the segment j places from the growing end loses about 2·3j blocks, and new segments are made at the far end. When a segment runs out the end segments merge (a collapse) and the drain starts over. An accelerated simulator runs past several collapses to 1019 steps without a halt. The collapses are not understood, so halting is undecided.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (E1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 99,142 cells have been visited and 42,433 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.489). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.062).

claims.title: 11 shift rules
claims.text: For every n, the head crosses n copies of a short word in a fixed number of steps per copy and leaves another word behind (for example the head going left over 0111 and leaving 0100, 18 steps a copy; these cross the 111-blocks of the counter). Generated and proved by bbtools.symtm, checked by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>19</sup> steps
claims.text: A macro simulator (blocks of 4 cells, crossing long runs of equal blocks in one go; it agrees with the direct simulator at 2×10<sup>9</sup> steps) runs 10,000,000,000,378,843,465 steps without a halt, through the collapses at about 3×10<sup>17</sup>.

claims.title: The draining law
claims.text: Between collapses, the segment j places from the growing end loses 2·3<sup>j</sup> blocks per cycle (6, 18, 54, 162, … per sampled cycle of the macro run), with occasional off-by-one irregularities at the junk near the ends. It is checked on the cycles of the direct run to 4.5×10<sup>9</sup> steps (failing exactly at the collapses) and on the macro run to 10<sup>19</sup>; the far-end rule that makes new segments is not pinned down.

claims.title: The next collapse
claims.text: At 10<sup>19</sup> steps the three segments next to the growing end hold 22,849, 4,261 and 3,351 blocks; the 4,261 runs out first, after about 240 more cycles; cycles have been getting longer by a factor of about 2 on average, so that is far beyond reach.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. Halting needs the head in state D on a 1 with a 1 to its right (D1 → 0RE, E1 halts); inside the draining regime this does not occur, and what a collapse does in general is not known.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Its tape is a list of counters, like an odometer read backwards: the counters near one end drain at rates 6, 18, 54, … while new ones are wound up at the other end. It has survived every collapse seen so far, up to 10<sup>19</sup> steps.

facts.text: No halt in an accelerated simulation, through several collapses.
The moves across the counter blocks, proved in Lean.
Blocks lost per cycle by the j-th segment from the growing end.

sections.heading: A list of counters that drain
html: Each time the head writes a new cell at the right end, the tape, read as lengths of runs of 1s from the far end, is 6 3^x1 9 3^x2 9 … 9 3^xm and a little junk: blocks 111 grouped into segments by markers of nine 1s. The numbers xi of blocks per segment are the state. The head sweeps over all of it, so the tape grows like the square root of the time on the far side and very slowly at the growing end.

Its mirror image 1RB---_0RC0LA_1LD0RB_1LE0LF_1RC1LF_0LC0LB is this machine started in state E, with left and right swapped and the states relabelled (A→E, B→D, C→A, D→B, E→C); the two runs follow the same law with different numbers.

sections.heading: Faster drains near the end
html: From one cycle to the next the segment next to the growing end loses 6 blocks, the one before it 18, then 54, 162, … (2·3j), like the wheels of an odometer turned backwards. New, very long segments appear at the far end. When a segment near the end runs out the last segments merge and the count starts again: a collapse. The jump in the table is a collapse: the two small segments vanish and the next ones take their place. The next one is far away: the 4,261 runs out first, after about 240 more cycles; cycles have been getting longer by a factor of about 2 on average, so that is far beyond reach.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.489). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.062).
After 109 steps the tape spans 99,142 cells (69,451 left of the start, 149 right), with a density of 1s of 0.428.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: A nested ternary counter like a draining odometer: segments of 111-blocks near the growing end lose 2·3<sup>j</sup> blocks per cycle while new segments are made at the far end; it survives the collapses seen so far and does not halt in 10<sup>19</sup> steps (accelerated simulation).
family: Nested ternary counter (segments drained at rates 2*3^j, mirrored pair)
